title: Off-Plan Presale: 3 Rules Before You Launch
seoTitle: Off-Plan Presale: 3 Rules Before You Launch
description: Every presale launch is a test of trust. Three rules for developers: never fake the visuals, earn the click with the buyer's own unit, and show every unit.
answer: Before a presale launch: never use visuals that are not built from the real project, since one mismatch destroys trust; earn the click by pointing buyers to their own unit, not generic lifestyle images; and show every unit and amenity in detail, because details create the confidence that closes.
body:
You are about to launch a presale. Before the first post goes out, you need three rules, and the third matters most.

Every presale launch is a test of trust. The buyer is deciding one thing: do I believe what I am seeing? Your visuals either earn that belief or destroy it.

## Rule 1: never fake the visuals

AI images are now almost free and very fast. That is exactly the trap. Any image that looks like your building but is not built from your building's real geometry is misleading, however beautiful it is.

Buyers do not forget. The first time someone notices a window that is not where the picture showed it, or a finish that differs from the sample board, trust is gone, and it does not come back. A presale without trust does not close. Every visual must come from the real project: real plans, real dimensions, real materials.

## Rule 2: earn the click, don't just chase attention

Attention moves fast, and today it is hard to tell one project from another. Try this: go online and browse the branded residences launching in Miami right now, one after the other. They look like they came from the same studio. Same images, same mood, same story. Close the browser and try to remember which was which. You cannot.

Your job is not to look prettier than the others. It is to understand where the buyer's attention really sits, and for most buyers it sits on something specific: their floor, their view, their kitchen. Generic hero images get scrolled past. Their own unit gets clicked, and the click is the first step toward a sale.

## Rule 3: show every unit and every amenity

This is the big one. Show every single unit, inch by inch, and every amenity in the building.

Many developers think that is a dream: too expensive, too complicated. It is not. The technology exists and works at every budget, from a 10-unit boutique building to a 2,000-unit development. Scale changes the workload, not the principle.

It matters because when buyers can see every unit in full detail, they stop imagining and start deciding. Imagination creates doubt. Detail creates confidence. Confidence closes.

## Three questions before you launch

1. Does every image you use represent the real building?
2. Does your marketing point buyers to their own unit?
3. Can a buyer see every unit, inch by inch, before signing?

If any answer is no, you are not ready to launch. If all three are yes, you are no longer selling a dream. You are selling certainty.
takeaways: A presale launch is a test of trust, and visuals decide it.
Never use AI or generic images that are not built from the real project.
Most launches look alike; the buyer's own unit is what earns the click.
Showing every unit and amenity turns imagination into confident decisions.
Check three things before launch: real visuals, unit-focused marketing, every unit visible.
faq: Can developers use AI-generated images for a presale?
Only if they are built from the project's real plans and materials. Images that do not match the real building mislead buyers and destroy trust when discovered.
Why do presale launches all look the same?
Many developers use the same lifestyle imagery and narrative, which makes projects hard to tell apart and easy to forget.
Is showing every unit affordable for small projects?
Yes. Current technology works from a 10-unit boutique building to a 2,000-unit development; only the workload changes.
